analysis:
The change is documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md gets a new 'Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation' section, a placement-rule note near head line 3635, and a rename of the Qwen35 TensorParallelSwitchLinear path. No code, config or deployment change is in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

Security-relevant claims the doc makes, for the next pass to verify against the code (not verified here):
- TB-002/TB-007: tensor-parallel collectives are 'sealed all-sum' over a keyed, authenticated data plane. Load agreement binds the registered fingerprint, plan, prompt policy, KV storage and prefix cache, and a peer with any other value is refused before weights are read. The artifact is fully verified (prepareGemma4ResidentSource) and tensor shapes are checked before any byte is read.
- T-041/A-001: Gemma TP prompt prefixes are stored per rank in a memory tier and the owner's encrypted SSD tier (Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix), with a sealed vote and confirmation between ranks. This widens prefix-cache coverage to a new model family and mode. The code must be checked to confirm it keeps the HMAC lookup tags, the cacheSalt scoping and the 30-minute TTL, with no prompt-derived plaintext metadata. The doc says the prefix cache is on by default in this build, so the T-041 sign-off and SEC-035 scope may need to cover this new storage path.
- Availability: per-rank memory is charged per request and gated against held lanes, and the doc says a rank stop ends both ranks after the same step.
- Placement: the 'fastest' choice depends on link and share probes that are self-reported by the peer. Whether those can be manipulated to steer placement is outside the supplied evidence.

The doc admits that speculative decoding, media and a measured activation floor are not built. It also marks performance figures as [INFERENCE]. The actual Gemma4 TP sources, NativeWorkerRuntime routing and the prefix code are not supplied, so conclusions about their controls are unverified.
